Subject: Ephemeral padding and autoscale rules — HelixWorks Dedicated sizing

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We dug into our Q2 telemetry and want to start the Dedicated sizing conversation. Our production workload has very spiky inference patterns tied to nightly batch enrichments and business-hour interactive queries. For next quarter we're planning a 3x peak uplift during batch windows (typically a 30-90 minute window) and frequent shorter spikes (5-15 minutes) during the day.

High-level asks:
- A firm proposal for committed GPUs + an ephemeral "padding" allowance for short bursts
- Autoscaling policy recommendations that minimize cold-start latency during short spikes
- Failure/fallback behavior (what happens if burst pool is exhausted)

I've attached a short telemetry snapshot (helix_telemetry_q2.png) and a calendar of peak windows. Can your team propose a pragmatic guardband policy and a mutual action plan?

Goal: nail down a sizing + operational SLA before our procurement kickoff on Aug 1.

Best,
Emma

Hi Emma / David,

Appreciate the telemetry — that's helpful. High-level proposal attached (provisioning-draft.pdf) but here's the summary so we can iterate quickly:

1) Committed slab: 12x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved), sized for your sustained interactive baseline.
2) Ephemeral padding: an elastic pool of up to 6 GPUs that can be consumed for short bursts (preemptible when capacity pressure occurs). Billing for ephemeral padding is metered at a higher per-hour rate and capped monthly.
3) Autoscale rules (recommended defaults):
   - Scale-up step: +1 GPU every 30s when queue depth > 20 and avg latency > 250ms
   - Warm-up/prewarm: keep one prewarmed instance per slab to reduce cold-start by ~40% for short spikes
   - Cooldown: 5 min after load drops below threshold before scale-down
   - Eviction order: ephemeral padding -> opportunistic slab -> reserved (never evict reserved)
4) Fallback plan: when ephemeral padding exhausted, requests route to a quantized model variant with controlled latency degradation; we also offer queued token-budget mode for non-interactive batches.

Action items:
- Rishi will map GPU slab granularity and prewarm cost estimates (ops impact).
- Karthik will validate autoscale triggers against your latency SLOs.
- Mina (me) will generate mutual action plan + draft SLO addendum for procurement.

I'll set a 30-minute sync for early next week. If the proposal looks ok we can include a short Ops runbook and DocuSign addendum into the procurement packet.

Thanks,
Mina

Mina / team,

Quick technical notes after looking at the telemetry:
- Slab granularity: for predictable prewarm behavior we'll propose 3-GPU slabs as the atomic prewarm unit (maps well to your model memory footprint). That means the ephemeral pool should be sized in multiples of 3 for minimal fragmentation.
- Prewarm cost: keeping one prewarmed GPU per slab reduces cold-start but adds ~4% baseline cost; for HelixWorks Q3 that equates to ~0.5 GPU-months — we should surface that to procurement.
- Prewarming approach: use lightweight KV-warming with a short synthetic workload to quickly fill model caches (reduces tail latency more than naive container prestarts).

I'll draft the slab->ephemeral mapping and run a quick sim against their Q2 histograms tomorrow.

-rishi

Team,

Couple of operational constraints to lock in before we present numbers:
- Eviction & prioritization: ephemeral padding must be first-to-evict; we should also define a hard eviction TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) to avoid oscillation when transient bursts repeat.
- Scale step granularity: +1 GPU / 30s is ok, but we should add a backoff multiplier when scale events >3 in a 15-minute window to avoid runaway.
- Preemption notice: expose a short webhook to HelixWorks so their orchestrator can gracefully degrade long-running batch jobs when preemption occurs.
- Cold-start percentile target: commit to 95th percentile warm-start latency <= 400ms for interactive paths; anything above must trigger a manual ops review.

I'll attach a quick slab mapping that aligns with the 3-GPU slab recommendation.

-ben
